stories.summary: The Omnibus Reform, adopted under Directive (EU) 2026/470, significantly narrows the scope of application of the Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) and the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CSDDD). Many companies will no longer be subject to the reporting and due diligence obligations under these

stories.title: FCA to regulate ESG ratings providers
stories.summary: The Financial Conduct Authority will require ESG ratings providers to secure authorisation starting in 2028. The regulator aims to bring more oversight to a market that has seen rapid growth. The move raises questions about how the reliability of ESG assessments will be guaranteed. Details are for subscribers.

stories.summary: Deloitte has launched Green Claim Navigator, an AI-powered solution intended to help companies detect greenwashing across websites, reports and packaging. The firm says the tool helps ensure compliance with new regulations like the EU’s Empowering Consumers directive. Companies are facing increasing pressure to substantiate their environmental claims.

stories.summary: Uganda Communications Commission (UCC) Executive Director Nyombi Thembo has urged businesses to embrace technology in corporate reporting while strengthening oversight, cybersecurity and data protection to safeguard the credibility of institutional information. stories.title: SEBI flags EKI Energy carbon credit revenue
stories.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India found EKI Energy Services recognised Rs 197.04 crore of revenue early. The regulator says distributing cookstoves did not complete contract obligations, as verification and delivery of carbon credits remained pending. The company counted the money before the work was finished.

stories.title: McKinsey estimates climate adaptation costs at $1.2 trillion
stories.summary: McKinsey Global Institute estimates that protecting assets from extreme heat, wildfires, drought and flooding could cost $1.2 trillion annually by 2050 under a 2°C warming scenario. The report identifies 20 measures to break barriers to this investment opportunity. The scale of the problem remains a trillion-dollar prospect.

stories.title: Verra coal retirement methodology wins ICVCM label
stories.summary: The Integrity Council for the Voluntary Carbon Market has approved Verra’s coal plant retirement methodology, VM0052, as meeting its Core Carbon Principles. Projects can earn credits for emissions avoided when coal plants close early. Each project must include a just transition plan for affected workers and communities.

stories.title: Gold Standard introduces 200-year biochar storage test
stories.summary: Gold Standard has published a methodology for biochar carbon removal requiring credits to reflect storage for at least 200 years. Projects must store five units of CO2 for every unit of activity emissions. The standard includes three compliance tracks based on the scale of the industrial units used.

stories.title: Verra's VM0052 Wins ICVCM Approval to Boost Coal Retirement Carbon Credits
stories.summary: Verra has received the first ICVCM approval for a methodology covering early coal plant retirement. Its VM0052 Version 1.1 allows eligible transition credits to carry the Core Carbon Principles (CCP) label, marking a major step for carbon finance and the energy transition. stories.title: Gabon sells 6 million forest carbon credits to SEFE
stories.summary: Gabon has agreed to sell 6 million forest carbon credits to the German state-owned energy company SEFE. The credits are certified under the ART-TREES standard and are eligible for aviation sector offsetting. The deal marks a step in the country's efforts to earn revenue from forest protection.

stories.title: Isometric launches service for EU carbon border checks
stories.summary: Isometric has launched a service to help exporters prepare emissions data for the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism. The offering combines expert support with artificial intelligence to assist companies facing a September 2027 deadline. The accuracy of the data could impact competitiveness as EU default carbon values increase.

stories.title: Isometric launches pre-verification service for CBAM
stories.summary: Isometric has launched Ready for CBAM to help exporters prepare emissions data for EU verification. The service covers six sectors, including cement and hydrogen. EU importers must submit their first declarations for 2026 imports by September 30, 2027. The mechanism is the EU carbon tax on imports.

stories.title: Carbon prices rise as supply tightens
stories.summary: European carbon prices have trended toward 90 EUR per tonne, supported by tighter allowance supply and gas market pressures. Carbon Market Watch expects a Q4 average of 86 EUR per tonne. CBAM is increasingly a financial obligation for importers, requiring reliable emissions data for compliance.

stories.title: EU negotiators to oppose new climate financing at COP31
stories.summary: EU negotiators at the COP31 summit in Turkey will oppose any new climate financing commitments. The bloc intends to focus on implementing existing deals and accelerating the phase-out of fossil fuels. European sources cited a lack of appetite for further financial obligations.

stories.title: EU maintains climate targets for COP31
stories.summary: The European Union will head to COP31 in Turkey with a focus on accelerating the fossil fuel phase-out and tripling renewable energy capacity. Brussels aims to move from political commitments to concrete implementation, without reopening deals already reached by the nearly 200 participating states.

stories.title: EU to push for faster fossil fuel phaseout at COP31
stories.summary: The European Commission stated the EU will push for faster global action on fossil fuel reduction and electrification at the COP31 summit. The bloc also intends to implement climate adaptation indicators agreed at COP30 and support a fair transition to cleaner economies.

stories.title: Circular economy group warns against waste afterthoughts
stories.summary: The Circular Economy Institute is calling for waste prevention and repair to be treated as a primary mechanism for reducing emissions at COP31. The group argues that decarbonizing energy alone will not address emissions embedded in extracted and purchased goods. The summit begins next week.

stories.title: CalRecycle updates SB 54 source reduction baseline
stories.summary: CalRecycle has updated its source reduction baseline for Senate Bill 54, which takes effect January 1, 2027. The law mandates that producers selling packaging in California must achieve a 25 percent reduction in plastic weight by 2032. Targets are based on 2023 data.

stories.title: EU Circular Economy Act delayed to December
stories.summary: The European Commission has pushed the presentation of its Circular Economy Act to December 2. The proposal is expected to harmonize extended producer responsibility schemes and amend the WEEE Directive to focus on critical raw materials. The agenda update confirms the new timeline.

stories.title: Retailers discard significant portions of returned stock
stories.summary: Research from ReBound Returns and Advanced Supply Chain finds half of retailers discard up to 40% of returned items. Only 27% of retailers divert most returns through circular routes. New EU regulations now ban the destruction of certain unsold consumer goods. Some items are still finding the bin.

stories.title: Somalia hosts first circular economy forum
stories.summary: Mogadishu hosted its first Circular Economy Forum to explore turning 2,000 tonnes of daily waste into economic opportunities. Organized by Horn Thrive Hub, the event focused on recycling and reuse initiatives. The city is looking for ways to make its trash pay for itself.

stories.title: WRAP report projects circular economy job growth
stories.summary: A WRAP report suggests that shifting to a circular economy could add 550,000 jobs and £93bn to the UK economy by 2035. The sector currently supports 559,000 jobs. The modelling assumes progress will be made, though the report does not specify how that progress is achieved.

stories.title: AZZ Inc. releases 2026 sustainability report
stories.summary: AZZ Inc. has released its 2026 Sustainability Report. CEO Tom Ferguson stated the company remains committed to integrating environmental, social and governance principles into its daily operations and long-term strategy. The report highlights the company's progress in creating value for its stakeholders and communities.

stories.title: Logitech initiates supply chain decarbonization
stories.summary: Logitech has launched the Chain Reaction initiative to decarbonize its supply chain. The program begins with 17 suppliers pooling their purchasing power to buy renewable electricity. The company is attempting to make its suppliers pay for their own power transitions.

stories.title: Norges Bank invests in Aypa Power
stories.summary: Norges Bank Investment Management has paid $300 million for a 10 percent stake in Aypa Power. The investment manager co-invested alongside Brookfield, which is acquiring the battery storage platform from Blackstone. The platform currently manages 6.5 GW of capacity.

stories.title: NBIM makes first direct battery storage investment
stories.summary: Norges Bank Investment Management has acquired a 10% stake in Aypa Power for $300 million. This marks the $2 trillion oil fund's first direct investment in battery storage. Aypa Power operates 6.5 GW of storage capacity and aims to assist in grid decarbonization.

stories.title: NLC India targets energy mix shift
stories.summary: NLC India Limited aims for an equal 50:50 mix of conventional and renewable energy by 2032. CMD Prasanna Kumar Acharya says the transition will balance power generation while supporting India's energy security. The company is currently planning how to reach that target.

stories.title: Vardhman sets green power and net-zero targets
stories.summary: Vardhman Textiles targets 60% green power by 2028 and net-zero emissions by 2045. The company also aims to cut freshwater use by 30% and landfill waste by 50% by 2030. It reported that 34% of its inputs were sourced sustainably in 2026.

stories.title: NTPC ESG score updated
stories.summary: NTPC has received an ESG score of 64.6 from SES ESG Research. The full details of the assessment are available for subscribers. Further details were thin in the open report.

stories.title: Study assesses light pollution in protected areas
stories.summary: A study in Kerala’s Western Ghats examines how artificial light at night affects wildlife in protected areas. Researchers assessed 21 locations to see how human settlements and tourism facilities influence nocturnal environments. Light is being studied for its impact on where animals move and how they hunt.

stories.title: SINBON reports emissions reduction
stories.summary: SINBON Electronics announced a 27.68% reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions in its 2025 Sustainability Report. The company also institutionalized sustainability governance and linked executive pay to ESG performance. Sustainability is now being used to drive corporate competitiveness.

research.title: NASA reveals a haunting skull hidden in Antarctica’s ice
research.summary: NASA satellites have captured an eerie, skull-shaped formation on a remote Antarctic island, but its haunting appearance conceals a troubling warning about melting glaciers. Unusually warm winter temperatures have exposed large areas of dark ice, potentially accelerating future melting and gradually transforming the skull's ghostly features.

research.summary: A massive landslide in Alaska triggered the second-highest tsunami ever recorded, sending water and debris 1,580 feet up a mountainside just hours after tourists visited the area.
